articles.title: Ad hoc scout: codyn rank clocks and a variance ratio from ecology, aimed at Q1
articles.dek: Community-dynamics metrics (Hallett et al., Methods in Ecology and Evolution 2016), run on a PROXY Y-9C dealer panel. US dealer volumes co-move (Schluter VR = 4.45 vs a cyclic-shift null of 0.44–2.00); foreign IHC volumes do not (VR = 0.73, inside the null). Rank clocks make the GS→JPM equity-revenue swap visible. Scout recommends it for the promote workflow; not started, awaiting Jared's pick.

articles.title: Ad hoc scout: Lovell proportionality finds a sticky JPM–GS swap that gets stronger after the market is removed
articles.dek: A valid, no-tuning alternative to Pearson on compositions (Lovell et al., PLoS Computational Biology 2015). On the PROXY equity-revenue panel, JPM–GS ρ = −0.698 (BH q = 0.021) and −0.882 after residualizing on market factors (q = 0.036); JPM–MS does not survive. Pearson overstates many 14-dealer pairs. Scout recommends it for the promote workflow; not started, awaiting Jared's pick.

articles.title: Secret sauce plans for changeforest, partykit, MARSS and InspectChangepoint
articles.dek: Exactly three avenues per method — Engineering, Math, and a new use on our data — grounded in the 11-10 and 11-11 runs. Top picks are all math: a dependence-aware changeforest test, time-series-valid partykit splits, a short-sample sticky label for the MARSS decomposition (a v0.1-era framework, not a forecast), and an Inspect procedure with the right size under persistent shares. Plans only.

articles.title: changeforest: a random forest that dates regime breaks, once you stop feeding it levels
articles.dek: Rust-core change-point detection that sees volatility and correlation breaks a mean test misses. Reproduced exactly in all three applications; recommended for promotion with a mandatory persistence check, awaiting Jared's approval.

articles.title: Weekly rate and stress regimes: 35 breaks, and a null that finds just as many
articles.dek: On weekly changes of six series the break dates reproduce exactly, but a stationary VAR(1) null produces 20–37 breaks too. Prewhitening leaves 12 stable breaks.

articles.title: Daily volatility and correlation regimes in 9,174 days of rates and VIX
articles.dek: 28 breaks, 23 stable across seeds, zero under both nulls, zero for a mean-change test: this is the use changeforest is built for.

articles.title: Credit spreads have had three regimes since 1990, split in Aug 1998 and Jul 2012
articles.dek: New application: monthly changes of the GZ spread, excess bond premium, VIX and the 10y. Two breaks, both stable, zero under both nulls.

articles.title: partykit trees: readable subgroups that pass on a cross-section and overfit time series
articles.dek: Conditional inference trees and model-based trees reproduced exactly. They clear every gate on 3,074 counties, but a circular-shift null breaks both time-series uses. Recommended (scoped), awaiting approval. A well-known package, so less of a scout find.

articles.title: A VIX-led regime tree for credit spreads: readable, stable, and not real enough
articles.dek: The 4-leaf tree reproduces exactly and VIX wins the root in about 70% of bootstraps. But a shifted response still splits 60% of the time, and the tree loses to the historical mean out of sample.

articles.title: When financial conditions tighten, credit spreads react twice as hard to VIX
articles.dek: A model-based tree splits once, at NFCI 0.057, and beats a calendar break. The catch: shifted state variables split 53% of the time too.

articles.title: Which counties took the biggest unemployment hits in 2008 and 2020
articles.dek: Great Recession damage sorted on pre-crisis unemployment; COVID damage sorted on county size. Both trees clear the null and stay within reach of OLS.

articles.title: Scout: MARSS splits dealer share moves into market, sticky and transient parts
articles.dek: State-space model from ecology (R Journal 2012), run on a PROXY Y-9C dealer-share panel for Q1. GS's equity-revenue-share loss is sticky and mirrors JPM's gain (corr −0.79, BH q = 0.04), while market factors drive 59–74% of quarterly swings for JPM, MS and BAC. Scout recommends it for the promote workflow; not started, awaiting Jared's pick.

articles.title: Scout: InspectChangepoint names which dealers moved at a break, but the breaks fail a persistence null
articles.dek: Sparse-projection change points (JRSS-B 2018), 9.6 ms per panel. On PROXY dealer shares, level breaks (8) are fewer than persistence-matched surrogates produce (12.4–13.3), and drift tests find no significant break: gradual migration, not shocks. Scout verdict: interesting.
